title: Transcriptomic Classification using Mixture of Normal Distributions
text: Cancer classification, using RNA sequencing, now part modern precision oncology. cancers, RNA classification provides deep insights tumor aggressiveness growth rates. example, breast cancer subtypes (like Luminal-, Luminal-B, HER2-enriched, Basal-like) help forecast patient outcomes (Cascianelli et al. 2020). Luminal-common molecular subtype breast cancer, making 60% breast cancer cases. also associated good prognosis, Luminal-B tumors aggressive phenotype worse prognosis (Yersal 2014). widely accepted major oncology organizations, gene signatures RNA subtyping used classify cancer subtypes, predict patient survival, guide treatment. research perspective, classification new samples using transcriptional profiles can done using different tools. cancers, machine learning models dedicated software available Bioconductor Genefu package breast cancer molecular subtyping (Gendoo et al. 2016), CMScaller package subtyping colorectal cancer (Eide et al. 2017). absence dedicated software, unsupervised clustering heatmap visualization classify transcriptomic samples gene signature often employed. method relatively simple offers instant visual support. However, method drawbacks: Lack statistical metrics: doesn’t provide statistical probability score sample’s class assignment; mainly acts visual summary. Metric sensitivity: Changing clustering metric (e.g., “Euclidean” “Pearson” distance) can alter resulting clusters. Outlier distortion: Extreme outliers can squash color scale, artificially create skewed subsets. splitTypeR package resolves issues providing automated statistical framework classify heterogeneous biological samples based gene signature lists, effectively isolating signature-positive samples. classification method designed bulk transcriptomic datasets.

(Tiriac et al. 2018).  86% samples (32 37) assigned subtype. following graph shows GSVA scores sample signatures. dashed lines represent classification threshold signature (95th percentile “low-mean” distribution). sample located right vertical line assigned classical signature, sample located horizontal line assigned basal-like signature. samples classification differs Tiriac et al. (Tiriac et al. 2018) labeled.   samples assigned subtype intermediate scores located classical basal-like samples meet. Sample hF50 located region signatures assigned therefore remains unclassified.
code: ## Assignments from Tiriac et al. pathAssign <- system.file("extdata", "Moffitt_Tiriac_2018_Assignation.txt",                         package="splitTypeR") tiriacAssign <- read.table(pathAssign, sep="\t", header=TRUE)  ## Assignments from the mixture model are extracted from the result ## By default, the samples are considered unclassified ## The samples are classified only if they are assigned to one of the signatures ## When assigned to both signatures, the samples remain unclassified assignation <- data.frame(         Samples=rownames(classification(result)[['Classical']]),          newAssignation="unclassified") assignation$Classical <- classification(result)[['Classical']]$classification assignation$Basal <- classification(result)[['Basal-like']]$classification assignation$newAssignation[which(assignation$Classical == "Classical" &                      assignation$Basal == "unclassified")] <- "Classical" assignation$newAssignation[which(assignation$Basal == "Basal-like" &                      assignation$Classical == "unclassified")] <- "Basal-like"  ## Merge the current assignments with the Tiriac et al. assignments into  ## one data frame assignation <- merge(assignation[, c("Samples", "newAssignation")],                          tiriacAssign, by.x="Samples",                          by.y="Line", all.y=FALSE, all.x=FALSE)  table(assignation$newAssignation, assignation$Moffitt) ##                ##                Basal-like Classical ##   Basal-like            8         3 ##   Classical             1        24 ##   unclassified          0         1 ## Required package library(ggplot2)  ## Get the GSVA score of each sample for both signatures gsva <- data.frame(     Samples=rownames(classification(result)[['Classical']]),     Classical=classification(result)[['Classical']]$GSVA_score,     Basal=classification(result)[['Basal-like']]$GSVA_score)  ## Add the assignments and identify the samples with a different ## classification than Tiriac et al. gsva <- merge(gsva, assignation, by="Samples") gsva$Agreement <- ifelse(gsva$newAssignation == gsva$Moffitt,     "Same classification", "Different classification")  ## Classification threshold of each signature thresholdClassical <- threshold(result)[['Classical']] thresholdBasal <- threshold(result)[['Basal-like']]  ## Scatter plot of the GSVA scores with the classification thresholds ## The vertical dashed line is the classical threshold and the horizontal ## dashed line is the basal-like threshold ggplot(gsva, aes(x=Classical, y=Basal)) +     geom_vline(xintercept=thresholdClassical, linetype="dashed",         color="gray40") +     geom_hline(yintercept=thresholdBasal, linetype="dashed",         color="gray40") +     geom_point(aes(color=Agreement, shape=Moffitt), size=3) +     geom_text(data=gsva[gsva$Agreement == "Different classification", ],         aes(label=Samples), vjust=-1, size=3.5) +     scale_color_manual(values=c("Same classification"="gray60",         "Different classification"="firebrick")) +     labs(x="GSVA score - Classical signature",         y="GSVA score - Basal-like signature",         color="Compared to Tiriac et al.", shape="Tiriac et al.") +     theme_bw()

code: ## Required library library(GSVA)  ## Load signatures data(signaturesDemo)  ## Create a list of two signatures geneLists <- list() geneLists[["classical"]] <-      signaturesDemo$`Classical` geneLists[["basal"]] <-      signaturesDemo$`Basal-like`  ## Load demo normalized expected counts data(expNormalCountsDemo)  ## Fix seed for reproducibility set.seed(144)  ## Calculate GSVA scores for the signatures gsvaParameter <- gsvaParam(exprData=as.matrix(expNormalCountsDemo),     geneSets=geneLists) resClass <- gsva(param=gsvaParameter, verbose=FALSE)  ## Calculate standard deviation for each sample using the permutation method permResult <- splitTypeR:::permuteGSVA(geneLists=geneLists,      countMatrix=expNormalCountsDemo, permRatio=0.75, permNbr=20)  ## For each sample, randomly select 10 values (nbValues) from the normal  ## curve where mean is the real GSVA value, and the standard deviation is  ## calculated from the permutation step. normResult <- splitTypeR:::extractFromNormalDist(geneLists=geneLists,      gsvaRes=resClass, gsvaSD=permResult$SD, nbValues=10)  ## Extracting the mixtures of two normal distributions for each signature model <- splitTypeR:::normalMix(geneLists=geneLists, resultNorm=normResult)  ## The two means of the normal distributions for the basal signature model[["basal"]]$mu #> [1] -0.5352405  0.3578356

code: ## Required library library(GSVA)  ## Load signatures data(signaturesDemo)  ## Create a list of two signatures geneLists <- list() geneLists[["classical"]] <-      signaturesDemo$`Classical` geneLists[["basal"]] <-      signaturesDemo$`Basal-like`  ## Load demo normalized expected counts data(expNormalCountsDemo)  gsvaParameter <- gsvaParam(exprData=as.matrix(expNormalCountsDemo),     geneSets=geneLists) resClass <- gsva(param=gsvaParameter, verbose=FALSE)  ## Calculate standard deviation for each sample using the permutation method permResult <- splitTypeR:::permuteGSVA(geneLists=geneLists,      countMatrix=expNormalCountsDemo, permRatio=0.75, permNbr=20)  ## Draw 10 values from the normal distribution for each sample (upscaling) normResult <- splitTypeR:::extractFromNormalDist(geneLists=geneLists,      gsvaRes=resClass, gsvaSD=permResult$SD, nbValues=10)  ## Obtain the mixtures of normal distributions for each signature model <- splitTypeR:::normalMix(geneLists=geneLists, resultNorm=normResult)  ## Obtain the assignment of each sample for each signature result <- splitTypeR:::sampleClassification(geneLists=geneLists,      gsvaRes=resClass, modelMix=model)      ## Assignment for the classical signature head(result$classical) #>           GSVA_score classification #> Patient_1  0.1422663   unclassified #> Patient_2  0.4274225      classical #> Patient_3 -0.7532768   unclassified #> Patient_4  0.3479971      classical #> Patient_5 -0.6732937   unclassified #> Patient_6  0.5735090      classical ## Assignment for the basal signature head(result$basal) #>           GSVA_score classification #> Patient_1 -0.2385417          basal #> Patient_2 -0.4403292   unclassified #> Patient_3  0.8006550          basal #> Patient_4 -0.4500838   unclassified #> Patient_5  0.8175287          basal #> Patient_6 -0.6076389   unclassified
